en: The Scripture Spoken by the Buddha on the Contemplation of the Two Bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata.
Translated during the Song Dynasty by the Tripiṭaka Master Guṇabhadra from the Western Regions (Song language: Shicheng).
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the country of Vaiśālī, in the Monkey Grove, amidst the blue...
At the Lotus Pond Hermitage,
he was together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
including the Venerable Mahākāśyapa.
The Venerable Śāriputra,
the Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana, and the Venerable Mahākātyāyana.
There were also ten thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, all well-known to such assemblies, who were present together with him. Their names were:
the Bodhisattva Wondrous Treasure Store (Miaodanzang), the one named Virtuous (Youde) with the epithet Arm (Zhibi), and so forth.
Bodhisattva Good Sound,
Bodhisattva Silent Sound,
and Bodhisattva Jewel Virtue.
The Bodhisattva Prajñāśrī, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
and the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
These were the foremost among them.
Furthermore, ten billion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas came from the ten directions,
including the Bodhisattva Bhadramukha.
The Qiantan edition reads "Cai" (才) at the beginning:
Bodhisattva [Cai], Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
and Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattva.
Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,
Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata,
and Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
The Bodhisattva Bhadrapāla,
the Bodhisattva Brahmādeva,
the Bodhisattva Brahmadhvaja, and others.
Furthermore, five hundred Licchavis from Vaiśālī were present together with the elder Candracchattra and the elder’s son Ratnākara; all had assembled there.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Samādhi of Universal Radiance.
From all the pores of his body, he emitted light of variegated colors,
which illuminated the Monkey Forest, making it appear the color of the seven treasures.
Light issued forth from above the grove and transformed into a precious canopy.
Within this canopy, all the rare and marvelous events of the worlds of the ten directions were fully manifested.
At that time, the elder’s son Ratnākara...
He immediately rose from his seat, went to where Ānanda was,
and said to him: "Venerable One, today the World-Honored One has entered into samādhi,
and his entire body emits light."
"He will surely preach the sublime Dharma;
we pray that the Venerable One will know it is time.
Ānanda replied:
When the son of the elder said, "The Buddha has entered samādhi;
I did not dare to invite him," at that moment, light radiated from the Buddha’s eyes.
It shone upon the crowns of the two bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata,
and remained above their heads like a mountain of adamant.
Within this mountain, all the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions were reflected.
These World-Honored Ones also emitted rays of light that universally illumined the crowns of the heads of all the bodhisattvas; upon their crowns,
[the light] appeared like mountains of lapis lazuli.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions who have attained the Śūraṅgama Samādhi cause this Mountain of Light to appear;
when this sign manifests, precious lotuses grow within Monkey Pond.
It is made of white jewel-colored substance;
its color is so pure and white that it is beyond all comparison.
Therein dwell various emanation Buddhas seated upon lotus flowers.
Their physical forms were subtle and wondrous as they also entered into samādhi;
each emitted rays of light that illuminated the crowns of the two bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata,
as well as the crowns of all the other bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One arose from samādhi and smiled with joyful serenity.
Five-colored light issued forth from the Buddha’s mouth.
As it illuminated his full moon-like face,
the Buddha’s countenance became twice as radiant,
surpassing his usual appearance by hundreds of thousands of millions of times.
The elder’s son Ratnākara, beholding the Buddha’s majestic appearance, marveled at such an unprecedented sight.
He immediately rose from his seat,
adjusted his robes, bared his right shoulder, and circumambulated the Buddha seven times.
Kneeling with palms joined, he gazed up at the Honored One’s countenance,
his eyes never wavering for a moment, and addressed the Buddha,
saying: “World-Honored One, Tathāgata, today you have emitted a great radiance.”
The Buddhas of the ten directions and all the Bodhisattvas have already gathered like clouds.
I wish to inquire briefly regarding the ocean of the Buddha-dharma.
“I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain this for me.
The Buddha told Ratnākara, “Ask whatever you wish.
Then Ratnākara addressed the Buddha, saying:
The World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, now emits light from his two eyes;
like a mountain of vajra,
it rests upon the crowns of the heads of the two bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata.
The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions were reflected upon Mount Kāñcanaprabha;
the majestic radiance of these two bodhisattvas was even more brilliant than a wish-fulfilling jewel.
They surpass other bodhisattvas by a factor of hundreds of thousands of millions.
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, during the time when the True Dharma is perishing,
if there are sentient beings who hear the names of these two bodhisattvas, how much merit will they obtain?
If good sons or good daughters wish to sever the karmic obstacles of transgressions,
how should they contemplate the physical marks and the radiance of the body of Bhaiṣajyarāja?
The Buddha told Ratnākara:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well.
I shall analyze and explain it for you."
When these words were spoken, five hundred sons of elders rose simultaneously and together prostrated before the Buddha;
each scattered blue lotuses as an offering over the Buddha.
"We wish to hear it with joy.
Then the great assembly gathered there and the various bodhisattvas,
with one voice and in unison, praised Ratnākara.
And he uttered these words: "Excellent, excellent, Ratnākara!

You are indeed able, for the sake of sentient beings who are blind and ignorant in future ages, to inquire of the Tathāgata regarding the dharma of the consecration of the wondrous medicine of ambrosia."
When these words had been spoken, they were all silent.
The Buddha said to Ratnākara:
"Sentient beings of the future will possess five causal conditions."
To hear the names of the two bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata— what are these five?
First, to have a mind of loving-kindness and refrain from killing.
First, they are fully endowed with the Buddha’s prohibitive precepts,
their dignified deportment being without deficiency.
Second, they filially support and nourish their parents.
Third, they practice the ten wholesome paths of worldly conduct; their body and mind are tranquil and serene,
and their mindfulness remains focused without distraction.
Fourth, upon hearing the Vaipulya sutras,
their minds are not startled or doubtful;
they do not sink or regress.
Fifth, one has faith that the Buddha is imperishable;
regarding the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), the mind is like a flowing stream, uninterrupted from moment to moment.
The Buddha said to Ratnakūṭa:
If there are sentient beings who possess these five conditions,
they shall always hear the names of these two Bodhisattvas in every place where they are born.
Furthermore, they hear the names of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions;
hearing the Vaipulya sutras, their minds are free from doubt and anxiety,
for they have heard the names of these two bodhisattvas.
By the power of his majestic spiritual authority,
in every place of rebirth for five hundred *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, he shall not fall into the evil realms.
When the Buddha spoke these words,
Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority,
then spoke this mantra: A-mu-kha (1), Ma-ha-mu-kha (2), Tso-le (3), Ma-ha-tso-le (4), To-shi (5),
Ma-ha-to-shi (6), Chang-ch’iu-li (7), Ma-ha-chang-ch’iu-li (8), O-mo-chih (9), Ma-...
Daśamai (20) dudu dudu (21) mahādudu (22) kāruṇika (23) daśarā svāhā (24) ajjukhu ajjukhu (25) maṇḍaki (26) padanti (27) cāti (28) svāhā.
Cāluka-ti (29), Buddhacāli (30), Kāruṇika (31), svāhā.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja...
Having spoken this mantra, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, such a divine mantra has been proclaimed by eighty billion Buddhas of the past."
The present Śākyamuni Buddha, as well as the thousand Buddhas of the future Bhadrakalpa, have also spoken this mantra.
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—
Those who hear this mantra, recite this mantra, and uphold this mantra will purify all karmic obstructions,
retributive obstructions, and afflictive obstructions,
which shall be swiftly eliminated.
While practicing various samādhis in their present bodies,
they behold the form-body of the Buddha in every thought-moment,
never forgetting the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Whether they be yakṣas, or pūtanas,
or rākṣasas, or kumbhāṇḍas, or kiṃkaras, or piśācas.
As for all evil spirits that consume the vital essence of humans and seek to cause harm,
there is no possibility of their success; even when one's life is about to end, [they shall have no power].
The Buddhas of the ten directions will all come to welcome them,
and they shall be reborn at will in the pure lands of other regions.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, saying:
Excellent, excellent, son of good family! You have skillfully spoken this mantra.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time also speak this mantra;
I too feel deep sympathetic joy for this mantra.
At that time, Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva also spoke a mantra before the Buddha, saying:

1. Naṇamū e 2. Fu yin fu huí fú 3. Liú fú qiú liú fú qiú 4. Kāli-ni-kā 5. Dī-mū dī-mū kāli-ni-kā 6. Vitti vitti 7. Kāli-ni-kā 8. Abhi-tti-tha 9. Abhita abhita 10. Kāli-ni-kā 11. Sañcarā svāhā Having spoken this mantra, Bhaiṣajyarāja Bodhisattva concluded.
He addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, I now, before the Tathāgata, shall proclaim this Consecration Dhāraṇī for Subduing the Ocean of Afflictions.
This dhāraṇī mantra..."
This has been proclaimed by all the Buddhas of the three periods of time. Should there be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
or upāsikās who hear this dhāraṇī, recite this dhāraṇī, or uphold this dhāraṇī.
One obtains ten benefits of merit. What are these ten?
First, because of the majestic spiritual power of this mantra.
First, the sin of taking life shall swiftly be purified.
Second, all ill repute resulting from the violation of precepts shall be entirely extinguished.
Third, neither humans nor non-humans shall find an opportunity to cause them harm.
Fourth, whatever they recite, contemplate, or memorize shall not be forgotten,
just like Ānanda. Fifth,
they will be revered by Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors, and all the devas.
Sixth, they are revered by kings and ministers.
Seventh, they cannot be defeated or subdued by the ninety-five kinds of heterodox teachers.
Eighth, their minds dwell in meditative concentration and they take no pleasure in worldly delights.
Ninth, one is protected and remembered by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions,
and all Śrāvakas come to consult with and receive teachings from them.
Tenth, at the time of death, one completely purifies karmic obstacles.
The Buddhas of the ten directions emit golden light and all come to welcome them,
preaching the sublime Dharma for them;
they are then reborn at will in pure Buddha-lands.
When the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja had finished reciting this mantra,
he joined his palms in reverence, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to stand to one side. At that time,
the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, saying:
Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You have well spoken this mantra.
The Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time also speak this mantra.
"I now rejoice with you from the depths of my heart.
Then, having spoken this mantra, the two bodhisattvas each removed their precious necklaces to offer them to the Buddha.
The necklaces scattered by the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja rested upon the right shoulder of the Buddha like Mount Sumeru;
the necklaces scattered by the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata likewise remained there.
A Mount Sumeru rested upon the left shoulder of the Buddha.
Upon the peaks of two mountains were palaces of the Brahmā kings,
where hundreds of thousands of millions of Brahmā deva-kings resided.
He stood in attendance with palms joined in reverence.
Within the palace was a precious lotus flower,
like a mani-jewel, which completely covered the trichiliocosm.
Suddenly descending upon the palace wall,
they merged into one like a thousand-petaled golden lotus.
It remained within the palace wall, and the Buddhas of the ten directions sat upon the golden lotus.
In the eastern direction is the Buddha named Sumerudīpaprabha.
In the southeastern direction is the Buddha named Ratnagarbhavyūha.
In the southern direction is the Buddha named Candanamaṇiprabha.
In the southwest is the Buddha named Sovereign King of the Golden Ocean;
in the west is the Buddha named King of Great Compassionate Radiance;
in the northwest is the Buddha named Victorious Blue Lotus.
In the north is the Buddha named Padmakośavyūharāja;
in the northeast is the Buddha named Vajradṛḍhavikrāntagāmīrāja; in the zenith is the Buddha named Viśiṣṭacandrarāja.
Below, the Buddha named Sūryacandraprabharāja—
thus do the Buddhas of the ten directions, with one voice and in unison,
praise the two bodhisattvas Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, saying:
The mantras you have spoken were proclaimed by all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
When we ourselves practiced the bodhisattva path in the past, [we likewise taught them].
Upon hearing this mantra, they shall rejoice with a profound heart.
By the power of the causal conditions of these roots of goodness born of such rejoicing,
they will immediately transcend the offenses of birth and death for five hundred and ninety-six billion kalpas.
Now, in the present, you have attained Buddhahood.
If there are sentient beings who hear the names of you two Bodhisattvas,
as well as the names of us Buddhas of the ten directions, [they shall attain liberation].
One will immediately attain the eradication of the sins of birth and death accumulated over hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas;
how much more so for those who receive, uphold, read, recite, prostrate to, and make offerings to it.
At that time, after the Buddhas of the ten directions had spoken these words, [the assembly rejoiced].
As he sat silently, having entered meditative absorption,
at that time Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the great assembly, saying:
"Do you now see these two bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata?"
"Is it not so that he stands before me with palms joined, making offerings with precious necklaces?
At that time, the great assembly, with Maitreya at their head, addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, indeed; we have already seen him."
The Buddha told Maitreya Ajita: "This Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja has long cultivated pure conduct, and his various vows are already fulfilled.
In a future age, after incalculable kalpas have passed..."

You shall attain Buddhahood, known by the name Pure-Eyed Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
The land was named Constant Peace and Joyful Light,
and the eon was named Supreme Fulfillment.
When that Buddha appeared, the ground became the color of diamond, like white jewels, extending down to the adamantine base.
From the sky, white jewel flowers fell naturally, perfectly round and fifty *yojanas* in diameter, filling that land entirely.
The sentient beings of that realm were free from physical or mental illness; the devas presented them with ambrosia (*amṛta*), yet they did not consume it as food.
They exclusively partake of the flavor of the unsurpassed Mahāyāna Dharma.
That Buddha’s lifespan shall be five million billion asaṃkhyeya kalpas,
and his True Dharma shall remain in the world for four million asaṃkhyeya kalpas.
The Semblance Dharma shall remain in the world for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of asaṃkhyeya kalpas.
Those born in that land will all abide in the gates of dhāraṇī,
maintaining mindfulness and concentration without forgetfulness.
After the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja had received his prediction,
he rose from his seat, leaped into the air, and performed eighteen miraculous transformations.
Descending from above, he scattered flowers over the Buddha.
The scattered flowers stood suspended in the air like a grove of golden flowers.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Maitreya:
"This Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata follows after Bhaiṣajyarāja."
He shall attain Buddhahood,
known by the name Tathāgata Viśuddhagarbha, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttarapuruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān.
When the Tathāgata Viśuddhagarbha appeared in the world,
this white jewel ground transformed into gold;
golden flowers and golden light filled the entire world.
All the sentient beings in that land are fully endowed with the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
The lifespan of the Tathāgata Viśuddhagarbha is sixty-two minor kalpas,
and his True Dharma remains in the world for one hundred and twenty minor kalpas.
The Semblance Dharma will remain in the world for five hundred and sixty minor kalpas.
At that time, having heard his prediction of enlightenment,
the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja immediately entered samādhi and manifested as a flower.
Like a campaka grove adorned with the seven treasures,
it was transformed into clouds of flowers;
with these clouds of flowers, they made offerings to the Buddha.
At that time, golden light was emitted from within the flower-clouds.
From within the golden light, beryl clouds emerged, and from within the beryl clouds, these verses were spoken:
"The World-Honored One, the Perfectly All-Knowing One, The stainless Lion of the Śākyas."
Peerless throughout the ten directions, The light of wisdom illuminates all;
Universally compassionate toward all beings, You have appeared in this world—
I now prostrate with head and face To the Great Compassionate One and the Three Applications of Mindfulness.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja had spoken these verses, he returned once more to his original seat.
The Buddha then addressed the great assembly:
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, if there are sentient beings who focus their mindfulness and contemplate the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,
they should form five perceptions.
First, the perception of counting the breaths while binding the mindfulness;
second, the perception of stabilizing the mind;
third, the perception of not exhaling.
Fourth is the perception of mindfulness of the true mark.
Fifth is the perception of abiding securely in samādhi.
The Buddha told Maitreya:
If good sons and good daughters cultivate these five perceptions,
they shall behold the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja within a single thought-moment.
The body of this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja is twelve yojanas in height;
however, according to the needs of sentient beings, it may appear as eighteen zhang or eight chi.
His body is purple-gold in color, possessing the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs of excellence, no different from those of a Buddha.
Upon the uṣṇīṣa at the crown of his head are fourteen maṇi jewels; each jewel has fourteen facets,
and between each facet are fourteen flowers.
He wears a majestic celestial crown.
Within that crown, the Buddhas of the ten directions and all the Bodhisattvas are clearly reflected,
appearing as if set within a multitude of jewels.
The tuft of hair between his eyebrows is the color of white lapis lazuli;
it encircles his body seven times like a white jeweled canopy.
From all the pores of his body, rays of light stream forth.
There were eighty-four thousand mani jewels,
each one of which turned and rotated to the right,
like the utpala flowers adorning a city of seven treasures.
Upon each flower was a manifested Buddha,
with a square body sixteen feet tall, like Śākyamuni;
each Tathāgata had five hundred bodhisattvas serving as attendants.
The two long arms of this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja are the color of a hundred jewels.
From the tips of his ten fingers, he rains down all kinds of the seven treasures.
If there are sentient beings who gaze upon the tips of this Bodhisattva’s ten fingers, [they shall attain liberation].
The four hundred and four diseases were naturally eliminated;
all afflictions of the body ceased to arise.
From beneath both his feet, vajra-jewels rained down.
Each and every jewel transformed into a cloud-palace,
within which were manifested bodhisattvas with countless devas serving as their attendants.
At that time, the manifested bodhisattva expounds the Four Noble Truths— suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self—
and also teaches the profound practices of the bodhisattvas.
When this visualization is accomplished, it is called the first contemplation on the meritorious marks and characteristics of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
In the second contemplation, the mind gradually expands and one beholds the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja with his complete physical marks.
At that time, the mind of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja is like a sandalwood maṇi jewel.
It is fully blossomed, pure, and possesses ten billion rays of light;
these rays encircle the body a hundred times,
like ten billion mountains of precious jewels.
Each of these mountains has ten billion jewel-foldings,
and within each folding there are ten billion transformation Buddhas,
their bodies adorned with all the marks and signs of excellence.
These emanated Buddhas, with one voice and in unison,
all together proclaimed the causal origins and practices of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
Whenever this sign appeared, in every moment of thought—
He saw the Buddhas of the ten directions preaching the Dharma to all practitioners according to their needs.
At that time, from every single pore of his body,
the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja emitted billions of light rays from mani-jewels, illuminating all the practitioners.
Having seen this, the practitioner attains purity of the six sense faculties;
immediately thereafter, they behold five hundred trillion nayutas of Buddhas and various Bodhisattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
For their sake, he preached the sublime medicine of ambrosia that eliminates transgressions;
having taken this medicine, they immediately all attained five hundred million *dhāraṇī* gates.
This was due to the power of the original vows of the Medicine King Bodhisattva.
Because they contemplate the self-adornment of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,
the Buddhas of the ten directions and the various bodhisattvas appear before the practitioner and expound for them the profound six pāramitās.
At that time, because the practitioner has seen the various Buddhas,
they immediately attain hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of ocean-gates of the samādhis for contemplating the Buddha.
The Buddha said to Maitreya:
After my parinirvāṇa, whether they be devas, spirits, or nāgas; or bhikṣus,
bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās— should any among them wish to see the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja or desire to keep the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja in mind, [they should...]
One should cultivate two kinds of pure conduct:
first, generating the bodhicitta and possessing the bodhisattva precepts with unimpaired dignified demeanor.
Because they have attained the full perfection of the bodhisattva precepts,
the bodhisattva companions from the worlds of the ten directions will assemble simultaneously and stand before that person.
Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja served as his preceptor;
for the practitioner, Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja then expounded hundreds of thousands of millions of koṭis of revolving dhāraṇī gates.
By virtue of having heard this dhāraṇī,
one transcends the offenses of birth and death for ninety billion kalpas and immediately attains the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
Second, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, all ordinary beings are bound by afflictions.
If any wish to see the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,
they should cultivate four dharmas.
First, with a mind of loving-kindness, one does not kill and does not commit the ten evil deeds;
one constantly contemplates the Mahāyāna so that the mind never forgets it,
and practices with diligent vigor as if one's head were on fire.
Second, one should provide the four types of offerings to teachers,
parents, and others: ghee lamps, oil lamps, *sumana* flower oil lamps,
and illumination provided by bamboo or wood fires.
Furthermore, they used ghee lamps, oil lamps, jasmine-flower oil lamps, and various other illuminations to make offerings to the Buddha,
the Dharma, and the Sangha, as well as to those who preach the Dharma.
Third, they deeply cultivate meditative concentration and delight in practices of seclusion;
they constantly prefer dwelling among burial mounds, beneath trees, or in forest hermitages (*āraṇya*),
remaining alone in quietude to diligently practice the twelve profound dhūta ascetic virtues.
Fourth, one completely relinquishes body, life, and wealth, giving rise to no attachment toward them.
For one who practices this dharma, in every thought-moment,
they shall behold the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, who will preach the Dharma for them.
Or, in a dream, they may see the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja bestowing upon them the medicine of the Dharma;
having awakened, they immediately recall their past lives through immeasurable hundreds and thousands of births, and their hearts are filled with great joy.
One should immediately enter the stupa to contemplate the image and pay homage.
Before the image, one shall attain the ocean-like samādhi of contemplating the Buddha and behold the assembly of immeasurable bodhisattvas.
They saw only the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja preaching the Dharma for them.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"After my parinirvāṇa, if there are members of the fourfold assembly..."
Those who can contemplate the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja in this manner,
and those who can uphold the name of the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,
shall eliminate the karmic offenses of birth and death accumulated over eight hundred thousand kalpas.
If one can invoke the name of this Medicine King Bodhisattva and worship with single-minded devotion,
one shall not encounter calamity or misfortune,
nor shall one ever die an untimely death.
If there are sentient beings who, after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa,
are able to contemplate in this manner, this is called right contemplation;
if they contemplate otherwise, it is called wrong contemplation.
The Buddha told Maitreya: "After my parinirvāṇa, if there are members of the fourfold assembly who wish to contemplate the pure physical body of this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja, how should they do so?
If they wish to contemplate it, they should cultivate seven dharmas."
What are the seven? First,
they always delight in upholding the precepts and never draw near to śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas.
Second, they constantly cultivate both mundane wholesome dharmas and supramundane wholesome dharmas.
Third, their minds are like the earth, giving rise to no arrogance,
and they extend universal compassion to all.
Fourth, the mind is free from attachment, indestructible like a vajra.
Fifth, one abides in the dharma of equanimity without abandoning dignified deportment.
Sixth, one constantly cultivates vipaśyanā.
They cultivate śamatha with a mind free from weariness.
Seventh, they have no fear or doubt regarding the great liberation of the prajñāpāramitā.
The Buddha said to Maitreya:
If there are good men or good women who possess this Dharma,
they will swiftly behold the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
The body of this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja is sixteen yojanas in height and is the color of purple gold;
the radiance of his entire body is like the color of Jāmbūnada gold.
Within the circular halo, there were sixteen hundred million transformation Buddhas,
each eight feet tall with a square body, sitting in the full lotus posture upon precious lotus flowers.
Each of these transformation Buddhas has sixteen bodhisattvas as attendants;
each holds a white flower and follows the light, circling to the right.
Within the light pervading their entire bodies, there are worlds of the ten directions.
All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and all pure lands appear within it.
The uṣṇīṣa on his crown is like a śakrābhilagna maṇi-jewel;
from the four sides of the uṣṇīṣa, golden light radiates forth.
Within each ray of light are four jewel-flowers, possessing the colors of a hundred jewels.
Upon each flower are transformation Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
appearing and disappearing in numbers beyond reckoning.
This Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja possesses the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs of excellence.
Within each major mark there is light of five colors;
within each minor sign there are hundreds of thousands of rays of light.
The tuft of hair between his eyebrows was the color of Jāmbūnada gold.
He wore a necklace of hundreds of thousands of white precious jewels,
each individual jewel emitting the radiance of a hundred kinds of gems.
Adorned with golden filaments like crystal banners,
it contains images of pure gold, wondrous and precious to the world;
all manner of ornaments appear within it.
If there are members of the fourfold assembly who hear the name of this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,
who uphold the name of this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja,
or who recite the name of this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
Regarding those who contemplate the body of this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja:
this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja emits light from his body to gather in and sustain those people.
This Bodhisattva’s light may take the form of Maheśvara or the form of Brahmā.
Sometimes he manifests in the form of a Māra-deva, sometimes in the form of Śakra;
sometimes in the form of one of the Four Heavenly Kings, or in the form of an asura;
sometimes in the form of a gandharva, or in the form of a kiṃnara.
Sometimes they manifest in the form of mahoragas;
sometimes in the form of garuḍas;
sometimes in the form of humans or non-humans; and sometimes in the form of nāgas.
Some take the form of emperors, some the form of high ministers,
some the form of elders,
and some the form of lay devotees.
Sometimes appearing in the form of a śramaṇa, sometimes in the form of a brāhmaṇa;
sometimes in the form of a ṛṣi, or in the form of one's grandparents;
or in the form of one's parents, or in the form of one's brothers, sisters, beloved wife, children, and various other kinsmen.
Or appearing in the form of a skilled physician, or in the form of a virtuous friend;
at that time, the practitioner shall, within a dream,
see these aforementioned figures appear before them and preach the divine mantras taught by Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata.
One immediately attains the eradication of the offenses mentioned above for as many eons as specified.
Having awakened, one remembers and maintains them, never forgetting;
with mindfulness fixed upon samādhi, one remains within that very concentration.
Upon beholding the pure and wondrous physical body of Bhaiṣajyasamudgata Bodhisattva,
he then proclaimed for the practitioner the names of the fifty-three Buddhas of the past,
saying: "O son of the Dharma, in the past there were Buddhas."
The first was named Universal Radiance; the next was named Universal Illumination;
the next was named Universal Tranquility; the next was named Tamālapatra-candana Fragrance;
the next was named Candana Light; and the next was named Maṇi Banner.
Next is named *Ratnakūṭa-ānandagarbha*; next is named *Sarvalokapriyadarśana-mahāvīrya*;
next is named *Maṇidhvaja-pradīpa*; next is named *Prajñā-ulka-daśadik-prabhāsvara*.
Next is named Ocean-like Virtue Radiance; next is named Vajra Firmness Universally Scattering Golden Light;
next is named Great Powerful Diligence and Valor; next is named Great Compassion Radiance.
Next was named King Maitrībala; next, Maitreyagarbha; next, Candanaguhanirbhāsaśrī; next, Bhadraśrī;
next, Sumati; and next, Viśuddhavyūharāja—these were the twenty.
Next is named Golden Flower Radiance; next is named Sovereign King of the Jewel Canopy Illuminating Space;
next is named Radiance of the Jewel Flower of Space; and next is named King Adorned with Lapis Lazuli.
Next is named Universal Manifestation of Physical Form Light; next is named Immovable Wisdom Light;
next is named Subduing All Demon Kings; next is named Talented Radiance;
next is named Supreme Wisdom; and next is named Maitreya Seer Light—these are the thirty.
Next is named Lokaprabhāsa; next is named Śāntamati-candraruta-varaghoṣeśvararāja;
next is named Nāgottama-jñānavikrānta-rāja; next is named Sūryacandraprabha.
Next is named Moon-Sun-Jewel-Light; next is named Supreme King of the Wisdom Banner;
next is named Sovereign Power of Lion’s Roar; next is named Supreme Wondrous Sound;
next is named Constant Light Banner; and next is named Lamp of Contemplating the World—these are forty.
Next is named King of the Lamp of Wisdom’s Majesty; next is named King of Dharma Victory;
next is named Sumeru Light; next is named Sumanā Flower Light;
next is named Udumbara Flower.
The Victorious King of Excellence was followed by the King of Great Wisdom-Power;
next was the Joyful Light of Akṣobhya; next was the King of Immeasurable Sound;
next was Talented Light; and next was Golden Ocean Light—fifty in all.
Next is named Sāgarabuddhivikrīḍitābhijñārāja; next is named Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū; next is named Sarvadharmasatatasamitābhyudgatarāja Buddha.
When the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja had finished reciting these names of the fifty-three past Buddhas, he remained silent.
At that time, while in meditative concentration, the practitioner beholds the seven World-Honored Buddhas of the past, beginning with Vipaśyin Buddha, who praise him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, son of good family! Those fifty-three Buddhas whom you have proclaimed—"
He was, in fact, one who resided in this Sahā world for a vast period in the distant past,
bringing sentient beings to maturity before entering parinirvāṇa.
Should there be any sons or daughters of good family, or any other sentient beings, [who encounter him...]
Those who hear the names of these fifty-three Buddhas will not fall into the evil realms for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.
Furthermore, if there are those who can recite the names of these fifty-three Buddhas, [they shall likewise attain such merit].
In every place where they are born, they shall always encounter the Buddhas of the ten directions. Furthermore,
if there are those who can reverently prostrate with a sincere heart to these fifty-three Buddhas,
their four grave offenses, the five heinous crimes, and their slandering of the Vaipulya sutras will be extinguished, and all shall become completely pure.
By virtue of the original vows of all these Buddhas,
in every moment of thought one immediately attains the eradication of all such sins as mentioned above.
This applies to Śikhin Tathāgata and Viśvabhū Tathāgata as well.
The Tathāgata Krakucchanda, the Tathāgata Kanakamuni, and the Tathāgata Kāśyapa also praised these names of the fifty-three Buddhas,
and likewise praised those good men and good women.
Those who are able to hear the names of these fifty-three Buddhas,
those who are able to recite their names, and those who are able to pay them homage,
shall have their karmic obstacles of sin eliminated as previously described.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the great assembly,
saying: "In the past, during incalculable kalpas ago,
at the end of the Dharma period of the Buddha Prabhāsa, I left the household life to study the Path."
Upon hearing the names of these fifty-three Buddhas,
having heard them, one joins the palms with a heart of joy and further teaches others so that they may hear and uphold them.
Having heard this, others instructed one another in turn until three thousand people had gathered;
these three thousand people spoke with one voice in unison.
Recite the names of the Buddhas and pay homage with a single-minded mind.
By the power of the merit and the causes and conditions of this reverent homage to the Buddhas,
one immediately transcends the offenses of birth and death for countless billions of kalpas.
These thousand Buddhas had Puṣpārāma-buddha as their first and Vipaśyin-buddha as their last;
they are the thousand Buddhas of the past who attained Buddhahood during the Kalpa of Adornment.
Regarding these one thousand Buddhas,
they begin with Krakucchanda Buddha and extend down to Ruci Tathāgata.
Within this Bhadrakalpa, they will attain Buddhahood in succession;
as for the subsequent thousand Buddhas,
Tathāgata Sūryaprabha shall be the first.
"Down to Sumukha, they shall attain Buddhahood during the Nakṣatra Kalpa.
Thus spoke the Buddha to Ratnākara.
The Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions, such as the Tathāgata Śubhavyūha and others,
have likewise heard the names of these fifty-three Buddhas and have each attained Buddhahood in their respective directions throughout the ten quarters.
If there are sentient beings who wish to eliminate the offenses of the four grave prohibitions;
who wish to repent for the five heinous crimes and the ten evil deeds;
or who wish to eliminate the extremely heavy offense of groundless slander of the Dharma—
One should diligently recite the mantras of the two Bodhisattvas, Superior Medicine King and Superior Medicine Upper;
one should also pay respectful homage to the superior Buddhas of the ten directions,
and furthermore, pay respectful homage to the Seven Buddhas of the Past.
Furthermore, one should pay homage to the fifty-three Buddhas;
one should also pay homage to the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa;
and one should further pay homage to the thirty-five Buddhas.
Thereafter, one should universally pay homage to all the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions.
Throughout the six periods of day and night, with a mind as clear and sharp as a flowing stream,
one should practice the method of repentance.
Thereafter, one should fix the mind upon the pure physical bodies of the two bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata.
If there are those who bring these two bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, to mind:
It should be known that this person has, throughout immeasurable kalpas in the past,
planted various roots of goodness in the presence of all Buddhas;
it is because they are adorned by the power of these original roots of goodness.
In a single thought-moment, he beholds countless Buddhas in the eastern direction.
At that time, all the Buddhas in the eastern direction simultaneously enter the Samādhi of the Universal Manifestation of the Physical Body.
The same was true for the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir;
they all likewise entered the Samādhi of the Universal Manifestation of the Physical Body.
At that moment, all the Buddhas of the ten directions...
All of them manifest their bodies and stand before the practitioner,
expounding for him the profound six pāramitās.
At that time, having seen all the Buddhas, the practitioner—
With a heart filled with joy,
he immediately attained the profound ocean-like samādhi of contemplating the Buddhas before all the Buddhas,
and beheld countless Buddhas.
Each of the World-Honored Ones, with one voice and in unison,
bestowed a prediction upon the practitioner, saying:
"Because you now keep these two bodhisattvas in mind,"
"In a future age, you shall attain Buddhahood.
At that time, having heard this prophecy,
the practitioner’s body and mind were filled with joy, and they immediately attained samādhi.
This samādhi is named Solely Unadorned.
By the power of this samādhi, one’s progress increases manifold,
and one universally beholds the countless Buddhas of the ten directions.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions may explain the dānapāramitā to the practitioner,
or explain the śīlapāramitā to the practitioner,
or explain the kṣāntipāramitā to the practitioner.
For some practitioners, he teaches the perfection of vigor (vīrya-pāramitā);
for some practitioners, he teaches the perfection of meditation (dhyāna-pāramitā);
and for some practitioners, he teaches the perfection of wisdom (prajñā-pāramitā).
For some practitioners, they teach the perfection of skillful means;
for some practitioners, they teach the perfection of aspiration;
and for some practitioners, they teach the perfection of power.
To some practitioners he teaches the perfection of wisdom;
to some practitioners he teaches loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity;
and to some practitioners he teaches the four foundations of mindfulness.
For some practitioners, he teaches the four right efforts;
for some practitioners, he teaches the four bases of psychic power;
for some practitioners, he teaches the five faculties.
For some practitioners, he teaches the five powers;
for some practitioners, he teaches the seven factors of enlightenment;
for some practitioners, he teaches the eightfold noble path.
For some practitioners he teaches the Noble Truth of Suffering;
for some practitioners he teaches the Noble Truth of the Origin;
for some practitioners he teaches the Noble Truth of Cessation.
For some practitioners he teaches the Noble Truths;
for some practitioners he teaches the Dharma of the Sixfold Reverence;
for some practitioners he teaches the Dharma of the Six Recollections.
In this manner, he extensively expounded various kinds of immeasurable Dharma gates through manifold distinctions.
Furthermore, by the power of the ocean-like adornment of this Samādhi of Contemplating Non-existence,
he extensively analyzed and explained for the practitioner the profound Dharma of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination.
By the power of the spiritual majesty of these two bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata,
he further beheld immeasurable Buddhas and bodhisattvas in the eastern direction,
their bodies the color of purple gold, with marks and signs of excellence beyond compare.
In the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below,
they likewise behold the bodily marks and secondary characteristics of each and every Tathāgata,
as extensively described in the *Buddhānusmṛti-samādhi-sāgara*.
If there are practitioners who recite the names of these two bodhisattvas, Medicine King and Medicine Superior;
or those who keep these two bodhisattvas in mind;
or those who uphold the names of these two bodhisattvas.
If there are those who contemplate the bodies of these two bodhisattvas,
or those who recite the dhāraṇī mantras spoken by these two bodhisattvas, they shall,
upon casting off this body, attain purity of the six sense faculties in a future life.
They will always be born into the family of great bodhisattvas;
their countenances will be dignified and handsome like those of Śakra, free from any unseemly features,
and their physical strength will be robust.
Like Nārāyaṇa, he subdues all;
wherever he is born, he always encounters Buddhas and Bodhisattvas and hears the profound Dharma.
Having heard it, he rejoices and immediately attains immeasurable gates of wondrous samādhi and dhāraṇīs.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "If there are sentient beings who merely hear the names of these two bodhisattvas, they will obtain immeasurable merit that is inexhaustible;
how much more so for those who fully practice according to the teaching."
At that time, Ānanda, having heard the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
praise the profound wisdom and immeasurable virtuous conduct of these two bodhisattvas,
immediately rose from his seat and circumambulated the Buddha seven times.
Kneeling with palms joined, he addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, what path did these two bodhisattvas,
Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, cultivate in past lives, and what merit did they plant?"
Now, within this assembly, he is praised by the Buddha like a Brahma-banner,
and is likewise extolled by the great multitude.
The Tathāgata now emits light from his two eyes.
"A mani jewel now appears upon his crown;
such a wondrous auspicious sign has never been seen before.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain for me the past causes and conditions of these two bodhisattvas."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well.
I shall now analyze and explain for you the past causes and conditions of these two bodhisattvas."
The Buddha told Ānanda: "In the distant past, immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago—
indeed, a number even more than that, beyond words—
there was a Buddha named Vaidūryaprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān."
The kalpa is named Perfect Peace and Security;
the land is named Suspended Banner of Excellence.
The lifespan of sentient beings born in that Buddha-land is eight great kalpas.
That Buddha, the World-Honored One, appeared in the world for sixteen great kalpas.
Only then did he enter parinirvāṇa in the Lotus Lecture Hall.
After the Buddha’s nirvāṇa, the True Dharma remained in the world for a full eight great kalpas.
The Semblance Dharma shall also remain in the world for eight great kalpas.
During this period of the Semblance Dharma, there will be one thousand bhikṣus who resolve their minds upon bodhicitta and seek the bodhisattva precepts.
He traveled everywhere to teach and transform sentient beings.
At that time, there was a bhikṣu among the assembly named Sūryagarbha.
Being intelligent and possessed of great wisdom, he traveled through villages,
hamlets, towns, and cities, as well as to monasteries, halls, pavilions, forest hermitages, and debating halls,
where he extensively praised the Mahāyāna and the fundamental life-stories of the bodhisattvas for the great assembly.
It was also spoken of as the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, pure, and equal Great Wisdom (*mahājñāna*).
At that time, there was among the assembly an elder named Jyotirprabha,
who heard this discourse on the Mahāyāna’s equal Great Wisdom.
With a heart full of joy, he rose from his seat,
took a harītakī fruit and various medicinal herbs,
went to where Sūryagarbha was, and said to him: "Venerable One," he declared.
"I have heard the nectar-like medicine spoken by you, O worthy one.
As you have said, those who take this medicine shall neither grow old nor die.
Having spoken these words, he prostrated himself with his head at the feet of the bhikṣu.
He then took this medicine and offered it to the bhikṣu,
saying, "Virtuous one, I now offer this medicine to you and to the assembly of Great Virtues.
At that time, Sūryagarbha performed a prayer of blessing and accepted the harītakī.
Having heard the Dharma and the verses of benediction, the elder’s heart was filled with great joy.
He prostrated himself before the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions and,
in the presence of Sūryagarbha, made this great vow, saying:
I have heard the Honorable One speak of the Buddha’s wisdom-medicine;
what you have said is true and not false.
I now take this excellent medicine from the Snowy Mountains and offer it to the Honorable One, as well as to the assembly of monks.
By this merit, may I, in birth after birth,
not seek the blessings and rewards of humans, devas, or the three realms;
rather, with a right mind, may I dedicate it toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
I now sincerely resolve upon the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment.
In a future age, I shall certainly attain Buddhahood.
This vow shall not be in vain; it shall surely be as the Buddha-wisdom described by the Venerable One.
When I attain the power of the purity of Bodhi,
although I have not yet become a Buddha, may any sentient beings who hear my name be granted the eradication of the three kinds of suffering and illness.
First, may the four hundred and four diseases within the bodies of sentient beings be cured simply by invoking my name.
Second, may they never again experience the suffering of wrong views, ignorance, and the evil realms.
When I become a Buddha, all sentient beings born in my land shall fully awaken to and understand the equal Mahāyāna, with no other paths remaining.
Third, within Jambudvīpa and in other directions, even the names of the three evil realms shall cease to exist.
Those who hear my name shall never again receive a body in the three evil realms;
even if they should fall into the evil realms, I shall ultimately not attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
If there are those who pay homage and maintain mindful contemplation of my physical form,
may these sentient beings eliminate the three obstructions,
becoming like pure lapis lazuli, transparent and radiant both within and without.
Seeing the Buddha’s form-body is likewise so.
If there are sentient beings who behold the Buddha’s pure form-body,
may these sentient beings never again fall away from the wisdom of equality.
Having made this vow,
he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground and paid homage to the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions.
Having paid homage to all the Buddhas,
he took pearl flowers and scattered them over the Sun-Treasury (Sūryagarbha), saying to the Upādhyāya: "Venerable One," he said.
Because of my preceptor,
I have been able to hear the unsurpassed, pure wisdom of the Buddha.
Having heard this, before my preceptor—
Since I have already resolved upon the profound *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
and this vow shall not be in vain as I will surely attain Buddhahood,
may these exquisite pearl flowers scattered by me [be transformed].
It transformed into a flower-canopy and hovered above the preceptor.

Having spoken these words, the scattered precious jewels became rows of jewel-lotuses suspended in mid-air, which then changed into a flower-canopy; that canopy was radiant, golden, and perfectly formed.
The entire assembly beheld this event and,
with one voice and in unison, praised the great elder Tārāprabha,
saying: "Excellent, excellent, O great elder!"
That you, within this great assembly,
have already been able to deeply give rise to such vast and great vows,
and thus manifest these subtle and wondrous auspicious signs.
"We who now behold these auspicious signs shall certainly attain Buddhahood; of this there is no doubt.
At that time, the elder Jyotīrasa...
There was a younger brother named Vidyutprabha.
Seeing his elder brother resolve upon the mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta),
he rejoiced with body and mind and said to him, "O elder brother."
"I now have a great deal of clarified butter and various excellent medicines in my home.
I pray that you, brother, will permit me to give them universally to all beings without restriction to the monastic community.
His elder brother replied, "I grant you permission; do as you wish."
At that time, the elder Vidyutprabha said to his elder brother,
"I too shall now follow my elder brother;
I wish to give rise to the profound mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
His elder brother replied: "If you wish to resolve your mind [on awakening],
you should now pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions before the Great Preceptor, the Bhikṣu Sūryagarbha."
"You should resolve to attain the profound and unsurpassed path of enlightenment.
The younger brother said to his elder brother,
"I shall now bestow this excellent medicine of *amṛta* upon all beings."
Furthermore, I offer exquisite flowers to the Buddhas of the ten directions.
I dedicate this merit, wishing that it may be no different from the vows made by my elder brother.
If my vow is sincere and not false, [may it be fulfilled].
He caused the exquisite lotus flowers he had scattered to remain suspended in the air like flowering trees. At that time,
the great assembly saw the lotus flowers scattered by the householder Vidyutprabha standing in rows within the sky.
Each individual flower was like a bodhi tree,
standing in rows in mid-air, fully endowed with flowers and fruit.
At that time, the great assembly spoke with one voice:
They all likewise praised the Elder Vidyutprabha, saying:
"The auspicious signs you now possess are no different from those of your elder brother; there is no doubt that in a future age you shall surely attain Buddhahood."
The Buddha told Ānanda, "You should now know that at that time,
the great elder offered *harītakī* and the superior medicinal herbs of the Snowy Mountains to the assembly of monks.
Having consumed them, the monks were able to hear the sublime Dharma."
By the power of the medicine, two kinds of ailments are eliminated:
first, the increase or decrease of the four great elements;
second, the afflictions of anger and resentment.
Because of this medicine,
the entire great assembly then resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and proclaimed these words:
"In future ages, we shall all attain Buddhahood."
At that time, the great assembly said to one another,
"Because of this Great Being’s gift of two kinds of medicine,
we have now been able to resolve our minds upon the supreme path of the Dharma King."
When you rule over the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system,
you shall establish a title for me as a token of gratitude;
because your name was established based on your conduct, you shall be named Bhaiṣajyarāja (Medicine King).
The Buddha told Ānanda: "You should now know that when this Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja heard the great assembly bestowing his name upon him,
he paid homage to the assembly and spoke these words."
"The Great Virtuous Sangha has bestowed upon me the name 'Medicine King.
I should now ensure that my reality accords with this name.
If I dedicate whatever I give toward the Buddha-way, it shall surely be accomplished."
May my two hands rain down all medicinal herbs;
may I rub and wash sentient beings to eliminate all their illnesses.
If there are any sentient beings who hear my name, [may they be freed from suffering].
Those who prostrate before me and those who contemplate the marks of my body—
may I cause them all to take this profound and wondrous dhāraṇī, the medicine of the unobstructed Dharma.
I shall cause all these evils to be removed from their present bodies, so that there is no wish that does not come to pass.
When I attain Buddhahood, I vow that all sentient beings shall be endowed with the practices of the Mahāyāna.
When these words were spoken, seven-jeweled canopies rained down from the sky, covering the King of Medicine.
From within the radiance of those canopies, a verse was uttered:
The Great Being, with sublime and excellent vows, Bestows medicine to save all beings;
In the future he shall attain Buddhahood, Named Pure Eye,
widely delivering gods and humans, With a heart of compassion that knows no bounds.
"With the eye of wisdom illuminating all, you shall become a Buddha in the future.
At that time, having heard this verse, the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja was filled with joy in body and mind, and immediately entered into samādhi.
The name of that samādhi is "Adorned Only by Emptiness.
By the power of this samādhi, one beholds countless Buddhas;
having purified and eliminated karmic obstructions, one immediately transcends the sins of birth and death for nine hundred trillion *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas.
The one who was given that title among the assembly at that time is none other than this present Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
The Buddha said to Ānanda: "At that time, you were he."

Knowing that his younger brother, the elder, was one who gave medicine as alms, people of the world praised him for this medicinal giving, saying: "This elder gives medicine to the Saṃgha and bestows it upon all."
Those who take this medicine obtain superior physical strength and attain the wondrous, supreme medicinal drugs;
they also hear the wondrous and supreme Dharma-medicine of the Mahāyāna.
At that time, people of the world gave him a name based on his conduct, calling him Bhaiṣajyasamudgata (Medicine Superior).
At that time, having heard all the people of the world praising his own virtue and calling him "Bhaiṣajyarāja," the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata then made this vow:
"In this world, for the sake of the entire great assembly..."
"Grant me the name 'Bhaiṣajyasamudgata.
I pray that when I attain the ten kinds of pure powers in future lives,
I may universally bestow the supreme medicine of the Dharma upon all beings."
May all sentient beings who hear my name have their flourishing afflictions swiftly extinguished.
If there are sentient beings who prostrate to me, invoke my name, or contemplate the marks of my body, [may they likewise attain liberation].
"May these beings be enabled to partake of this supreme, wondrous, deathless, liberating ambrosia,
the highest of medicines. When the great assembly heard these words,
each person removed their jeweled necklaces and scattered them over the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja.
The scattered necklaces remained suspended in mid-air like towers made of the seven treasures.
Within these towers was light of a pure golden hue,
and with voices like the Brahma-sound, they spoke these verses:
Excellent, O supreme mahāsattva! You have manifested your vast vows;
you shall certainly deliver sentient beings from suffering.
With no doubt in your mind, you shall in the future attain Buddhahood, and your name shall be known as Viśuddhagarbha (Pure Treasury).
"Protecting all the worlds who have sunk into the ocean of suffering," the Buddha told Ānanda: "Now you should listen attentively;
be careful not to forget the words of the Buddha."
These two bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata,
are the sons of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the past, present, and future, who have received the empowerment of their coronation.
If there are sentient beings who hear the names of these two bodhisattvas, [they shall attain liberation].
They shall forever cross the ocean of suffering and not fall back into birth and death;
they will constantly encounter all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas—
how much more so those who fully practice according to the teachings!
If there are good sons or good daughters who hear the divine spells spoken by these two bodhisattvas,
or who contemplate the physical marks and features of these two bodhisattvas.
In the present world, they will certainly behold Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata,
as well as me and the thousand Buddhas of this Bhadrakalpa;
in future worlds, they shall behold innumerable Buddhas.
Each World-Honored One preached the Dharma for them;
they were born into pure buddha-fields with firm resolve,
never regressing from their mind set on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, Ānanda rose from his seat,
prostrated before the Buddha, circumambulated him seven times,
and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, what should this sutra be named, and how should it be upheld?"
The Buddha told Ānanda, "Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well.
This essential dharma is named 'The Extinction of All Obstructive Karmas,' and it is also called 'The Divine Mantra for Repenting Evil Karma.'"

It is also called the sublime ambrosial medicine for curing the disease of afflictions, and it is also called the contemplation of the pure physical body of the Medicine King and the Superior Medicine.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "This is the essence of this Dharma."
There are such sublime and wondrous names as these.
After my parinirvāṇa, if there are bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs who hear this sutra and,
with a sincere heart, rejoice in it for even a brief moment.
The four grave evil karmas will all be completely purified.
If there are upāsakas or upāsikās who hear this sutra and, with a sincere heart,
rejoice in it for even a brief moment, then even if they have violated the five precepts, [they shall be purified].
One who breaks the eightfold fast will quickly attain purity,
whether they be kings, ministers, kṣatriyas,
householders, vaiśyas, śūdras, or brāhmaṇas.
Furthermore, all others who hear this sutra and,
for even a brief moment, rejoice with a sincere mind,
shall have their five heinous crimes and ten evil deeds entirely purified.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "This account of the original causes and conditions of Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata is a wholesome medicine for the illnesses of the people of Jambudvīpa.
When the World-Honored One had finished speaking these words, [he rose from his seat].
He remained silent, as if having entered into samādhi.
At that time, the elder’s son Ratnākara,
the Venerable Ānanda, and an immeasurable great assembly [were present].
Upon hearing what the Buddha had spoken, they all rejoiced greatly.
Because of this joy, five thousand people among the assembly of elders attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
There were also ten thousand bodhisattvas who had come from other directions.
Abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi,
five hundred bhikṣus who were disciples of Śāriputra became arhats, free from all outflows.
The eight classes of devas and nāgas were immeasurable in number,
and all gave rise to the aspiration for unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment.
At that time, the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, and the great assembly likewise did so.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced and practiced accordingly; they prostrated and withdrew.
This concludes the *Buddha-spoken Sūtra on the Contemplation of the Two Bodhisattvas, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata*.
